title: Behind the remittances: The social cost of the OFW economy

blocks.text: The overseas Filipino worker phenomenon reflects a structural economic failure that began 50 years ago, when what was intended as a temporary response to unemployment and economic pressure evolved into a permanent development strategy. To understand why the Philippines now has an entire Department of Migrant Workers (DMW), created in 2021, along with agencies and systems such as the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA), overseas employment certificates (OECs) and Philippine Overseas Labor Offices (POLOs), it is necessary to look back at how labor migration became embedded in the economy.
